meta.title: EGC — Context that never resets · persistent memory for AI coding tools
meta.desc: EGC is a local-first, open-source runtime that gives the 29 AI coding tools on your machine the same project memory, in every session.

hero.copy: EGC gives the AI tools on your machine the same project memory. Decisions, preferences and next steps come back in every session, in any tool.
ben.title: Why start over every time?
ben.lede: Close the window and the context is gone: your stack preferences, last week’s architecture decisions, the approach that failed after three attempts. Switch from Cursor to Claude Code and you start over again.
ben.voicesLabel: What you repeat every session without EGC
ben.v1: We use PostgreSQL with row-level security…
ben.v2: I prefer functional components, no classes…
ben.v3: We moved from Prisma to Drizzle because…
ben.figcap: Illustrative comparison: without EGC, the context available to the AI drops to zero at every new session; with EGC it is restored and builds up across sessions.
ben.c1: Context restored in every new session
demo.title: One decision, two tools.
demo.lede: Follow one decision: recorded in Cursor, kept by EGC and restored in Claude Code, without you repeating anything.
demo.badgeNote: A simulated interface that explains the flow. Not a real recording.
demo.d1: In Cursor you decide to switch ORMs. The AI saves the decision with store_decision.
demo.d2: You close the window. The decision stays encrypted in ~/.egc, on your machine.
demo.d3: Days later you open Claude Code on the same project and just say “let’s continue”.
demo.d4: EGC loads the project state and hands the decision to the new session.
demo.d5: The AI picks up where you left off, already knowing what was decided.
demo.uA1: Let’s move off Prisma and use Drizzle. Keep that.
demo.aiA1: Decision recorded for this project and branch.
demo.aiB1: I know the ORM is now Drizzle. Continuing the schema migration with it.
demo.reduced: Reduced motion is on: step through with the buttons.
fx.title: One brain, four faculties.
fx.lede: One local engine, on from the first install in every supported tool. Each circle in the mark is one of the parts working together for you.
f1.name: Memory
f1.title: What one agent learns, every agent knows.
f1.short: Decisions and lessons are kept and come back in any tool.
f1.body: Decisions, session context, working memory and learned lessons are captured as you work and are available in any terminal, IDE or agent. You speak naturally, in any language: “save this session”, “what did we decide about auth?”. There is no command to memorize.
f2.name: Session Mesh
f2.title: Your open sessions see each other.
f2.short: Parallel sessions announce what they’re on and cooperate instead of colliding.
f2.body: Two Cursor tabs, a Claude Code terminal and an Antigravity session share one live bus. They announce what they are working on, claim the files they edit and hand work to each other.
f3.name: Guardian
f3.title: Safety before every command.
f3.short: Risky commands and writes are checked before they run, in the background.
f3.body: Guardian validates commands before they run, gates risky writes and keeps context from overflowing, without you invoking anything.
f3.caveat: Caveat: coverage depends on each tool’s own hook support. The exceptions are documented in the project’s security assessment.
f3.proof: validate_command blocks shell injection · validate_write protects paths like ~/.ssh and /etc · validate_content flags prompt injection (advisory only)
f4.name: Token Crusher
f4.title: Noise never reaches the model.
f4.short: Long shell output is compressed by up to 90%, keeping errors and warnings.
f4.body: Before shell output reaches the model, Token Crusher compresses git logs, test spam, install noise and giant JSON while keeping every error and warning. Ask “how much did I save?” and the answer comes from your local ledger.
f4.proof: One 637 KB git log became 31 KB in a single crush · egc gain shows your own savings

ins.title: Two commands. No step three.
ins.st1p: Requires Node.js 20 or later. Works on Windows, macOS and Linux.
ins.st2p: Detects your tools, registers the local MCP servers and writes the memory protocol. It only asks whether you want the optional prompt library.
ins.st3p: Open your tool and say “let’s continue”. Memory loads on its own.
ins.npmNote: Linux, macOS and Windows. No git clone needed.
ins.req: Requires Node.js 20+ and git.
ins.reqWin: Requires Node.js 20+ and PowerShell.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions.
faq.more: Didn’t find what you were looking for?
q1: Does EGC send my project data anywhere?
a1: No. All state is stored locally in ~/.egc. Nothing is sent to external servers: the MCP servers talk over stdio only to the AI tool on your machine.
a2: 29 tools: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Antigravity, OpenCode, Devin Desktop, Amp, VS Code Copilot, Zed, Kiro, Trae, CodeBuddy, JetBrains Junie, Goose, OpenHands, Aider, Warp, Cline, Qwen Code, Kimi Code CLI, Crush, Auggie, Mistral Vibe, Grok Build, Kilo Code CLI, MiMo Code, Pi, Droid and Letta Code. The installer auto-detects which ones you have.
q3: Do I need to ask the AI to load context?
a3: No. egc install writes the memory protocol into each tool’s global instruction file, and the AI is told to load state at the start of every session. For tool versions that don’t read that file automatically, you may need to add it to the session context manually.
q4: How is this different from a CLAUDE.md or .cursorrules file?
a4: Those files are static and committed to the repo. EGC state is dynamic and project-local: the AI writes to it every session, building up decisions and preferences. They complement each other.
q5: Does it work with multiple projects?
a5: Yes. State is stored per project and per git branch. Each project gets its own memory.
a6: Yes. The engine is Apache-2.0 and stays free. If EGC ever offers something paid, it will be a team layer on top of the engine, never the memory on your machine.
a7: No. It is optional and off by default: the installer asks, and the engine (memory and Guardian) works the same without it.
cl.title: Same project. New session.
